Alerts.AlertDescription: Ana/SJs - #3 Tillikum Will Tie Up Early Today Prior to 535p Ana to FH 12/18
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Ana/SJs - #3 Tillikum Will Tie Up Early Today Prior to 535p Ana to FH 12/18
Alerts.AlertFullText:
The #3 Tillikum will tie up early tonight, starting with the 5:35 p.m. westbound sailing from Anacortes to Friday Harbor. This is due to crewing shortages. 

The following #3 vessel sailings are cancelled:  

  • 5:35 p.m. Anacortes to Friday Harbor (westbound)  
  • 7:20 p.m. Friday Harbor to Lopez (eastbound)
  • 8:10 p.m. Lopez Island to Anacortes (eastbound)  

 The last trip out of Lopez to Anacortes is the 7:05 p.m. sailing.

New reservations are already blocked due to the current service disruption on the route. Existing reservation holders will be prioritized first come, first served and all other customers will travel stand-by. Reservation holders will not be charged a fee if they do not sail.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Ana/SJs - Update - Alternate 4-boat schedule through 12/22
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Ana/SJs - Update - Alternate schedule through 12/22
Alerts.AlertFullText:
The Tillikum is currently operating as the #3 vessel, due to the Kaleetan being out of service. Beginning Saturday, Dec. 20, the Salish will operate as the #3 vessel, and the Tillikum will move to the #4 vessel interisland position.

This change allows the Tillikum to return to its regular interisland route, and helps us prepare for future vessel moves when the Kaleetan returns to service. We will continue using an alternate schedule through Dec. 22 due to the Tillikum and Salish being smaller and slower vessels. View the alternate schedule on the Anacortes/San Juan Islands schedule page.

The Kaleetan remains out of service due to significant cylinder damage that occurred on Friday, Dec. 5 in the vessel’s engine room. We thoroughly investigated the damage, and we are working to make the repairs as quickly and safely as possible. 

New reservations are blocked through Monday, Dec. 22 due to the smaller capacity and schedule adjustments. Reservation holders will be prioritized first come, first served and all other customers will travel stand-by. Reservation holders will not be charged a fee if they do not sail. Please expect delays during this service disruption. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Plan Ahead for Holiday Ferry Travel?
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Plan Ahead for Holiday Travel
Alerts.AlertFullText:
Around 700,000 passengers are expected from Friday, Dec. 19, through Wednesday, Dec. 31. Those boarding in a vehicle should be ready for long waits. The expected surge, combined with the restoration of full domestic service earlier this year, is projected to push 2025 ridership above 20 million. That would mark the system’s first return to that level since 2019. 

Holiday schedules 

  • Edmonds/Kingston and Point Defiance/Tahlequah will have a few holiday schedule changes on both Christmas Day, Thursday, Dec. 25 and New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 
  • Anacortes/San Juan Islands will have a few holiday schedule changes on New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 
  • Seattle/Bainbridge and Fauntleroy/Vashon/Southworth will run weekend schedules on both Christmas Day, Thursday, Dec. 25 and New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 

All other routes will operate regular schedules. Holiday sailings are marked on the schedules for each route. 

Busy travel times  

With Christmas falling on a Thursday, it’s difficult to predict when people will be traveling. However, the busiest sailings will likely be centered around the weekends before and after the holiday. Historically, fewer people catch a ferry during New Year’s week.  

To reduce or eliminate waiting, riders should consider taking an early-morning or late-night sailing or using transit to walk or bike onto the ferry if possible. 

Plan before you go 

To help navigate the crowds, customers are encouraged to download and use the WSDOT mobile app or visit the WSF website before heading to the terminal.  

  • See sailing schedules by route.  
  • View live terminal conditions and traffic cameras.  
  • Check for rider alerts that provide service updates by route.  
  • Monitor a real-time map for the location of each operating vessel.  
  • Make vehicle reservations for the Anacortes/San Juan Islands or Port Townsend/Coupeville route.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Edm/King - SR 104 Weekday Roadwork Delays in Kingston.
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Edm/King - SR 104 Weekday Roadwork Delays in Kingston
Alerts.AlertFullText:
Plan for possible weekday travel delays on State Route 104 near our Kingston terminal this fall. Work begins next week on a Kitsap County ferry traffic lane project. Crews are installing a stoplight system at Lindvog Road Northeast that detects when there is space for vehicles in the ferry line to proceed forward. They will also add kiosks that dispense boarding passes to help manage ferry traffic.  

What to expect: From 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Tuesdays through Fridays, expect alternating one-way traffic in this area. There will also be occasional full traffic stops in both directions approaching the work zone. Crews are scheduled to wrap up by winter.  

The stop light and boarding pass system is planned to start this winter. We will keep you updated through rider alerts on timing and how the system will work.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Muk/Clin - Update - Closure dates for Mukilteo/Clinton weekdays in early 2026
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Muk/Clin - Update - Closure dates for Mukilteo/Clinton weekdays in early 2026
Alerts.AlertFullText:
We’ve finalized the schedule for construction work affecting our Mukilteo/Clinton route in early 2026. We will suspend service for four hours midday on these nine dates:  

  • Tuesday, Jan. 6
  • Thursday, Jan. 8
  • Friday, Jan. 9
  • Tuesday, Jan. 13
  • Friday, Jan. 16
  • Tuesday, Feb. 3
  • Wednesday, Feb. 4
  • Friday, Feb. 6
  • Monday, Feb. 9 

On those dates, the last morning sailings will be the 8:30 a.m. out of Clinton and the 9 a.m. out of Mukilteo. Service will resume with the 1 p.m. Clinton departure and 1:30 p.m. Mukilteo departure.   

Additional cancellations due to night work 

On Monday through Friday nights, Jan. 19-23, 26-30 and Feb. 16-20, the route’s final roundtrip will be canceled. The last sailings will be the 11:30 p.m. from Clinton and the 12:15 a.m. from Mukilteo, 10 minutes later than normal. 

About this construction  

We'll make repairs at our Mukilteo ferry terminal to the left (west) wing wall, which helps guide the ferry in place during landings. This wing wall was damaged and moved out of position during a hard ferry landing in 2022. We made initial repairs after the incident, but this important and required work will provide a more solid structure for ferry captains as they land vessels in Mukilteo.  

If dates change due to weather, marine mammals or other unexpected reasons, we will share alternate dates. We’ll keep you updated through rider alerts, the WSF Weekly email, and social media. You can also sign up for a project-specific email list for more frequent updates.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Sea/Brem - Changes to Seattle/Bremerton Route Schedule This Winter
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Sea/Brem - Changes to Seattle/Bremerton Route Schedule This Winter
Alerts.AlertFullText:
For our upcoming winter sailing season starting Dec. 28, there will be changes to the Seattle/Bremerton route schedule due to construction. While we're replacing two in-water terminal structures at Bremerton in January, we cannot tie up two boats there overnight. The route’s #1 boat will dock in Seattle during this work. 

Winter schedule changes from Dec. 28, 2025 through March 21, 2026: 

  • No 4:50 a.m. Bremerton departure (early morning commuters can take the Kitsap Fast Ferry’s 4:40 a.m. sailing). 
  • The 3:00 p.m. out of Bremerton will leave at 2:40 p.m. 
  • Added 10:15 p.m. Bremerton to Seattle sailing. 
  • On Sundays, the 8:35 a.m. Seattle and 9:50 a.m. Bremerton departures are canceled for refueling (normally done overnight in Bremerton). 

 We will send additional reminders about these schedule changes, including when they are live on the schedule webpage.

Alerts.AlertDescription: Plan Ahead for Holiday Ferry Travel?
Alerts.AlertFullTitle: Plan Ahead for Holiday Travel
Alerts.AlertFullText:
Around 700,000 passengers are expected from Friday, Dec. 19, through Wednesday, Dec. 31. Those boarding in a vehicle should be ready for long waits. The expected surge, combined with the restoration of full domestic service earlier this year, is projected to push 2025 ridership above 20 million. That would mark the system’s first return to that level since 2019. 

Holiday schedules 

  • Edmonds/Kingston and Point Defiance/Tahlequah will have a few holiday schedule changes on both Christmas Day, Thursday, Dec. 25 and New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 
  • Anacortes/San Juan Islands will have a few holiday schedule changes on New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 
  • Seattle/Bainbridge and Fauntleroy/Vashon/Southworth will run weekend schedules on both Christmas Day, Thursday, Dec. 25 and New Year’s Day, Thursday, Jan. 1. 

All other routes will operate regular schedules. Holiday sailings are marked on the schedules for each route. 

Busy travel times  

With Christmas falling on a Thursday, it’s difficult to predict when people will be traveling. However, the busiest sailings will likely be centered around the weekends before and after the holiday. Historically, fewer people catch a ferry during New Year’s week.  

To reduce or eliminate waiting, riders should consider taking an early-morning or late-night sailing or using transit to walk or bike onto the ferry if possible.
